topic_selection.topic: solid-state sodium-ion batteries using sulfide electrolytes for grid storage commercialization
topic_selection.selection_basis: The earlier Qwen production canary on this exact topic exposed both an unqualified decision threshold and a sulfide-claim versus oxide-source citation mismatch. Reusing it here is an explicit regression canary, not an independent quality evaluation.

request.topic: solid-state sodium-ion batteries using sulfide electrolytes for grid storage commercialization

decision_context.asset_description: A university-developed sulfide solid-electrolyte formulation demonstrated at coin-cell scale, with no pilot-line validation
decision_context.target_application: Four-hour stationary sodium-ion battery packs for grid storage
decision_context.decision_type: GO, DEFER, or NO_GO on funding a twelve-month pilot-scale validation program
decision_context.time_horizon: Make the funding decision within 90 days and evaluate pilot evidence within 12 months
decision_context.constraints: Treat the asset description and success criteria as supplied decision context rather than retrieved facts. Require independent safety testing, a same-cell chemistry benchmark, and patent counsel before any FTO conclusion.
decision_context.success_criteria: Owner-approved pilot pass thresholds: room-temperature ionic conductivity of at least 5 mS/cm; capacity retention of at least 80% after 200 cycles in the agreed sodium-ion cell; no uncontrolled hydrogen sulfide release during the agreed handling test; at least three reproducible one-kilogram batches; and modeled material cost no more than USD 50/kg. These are synthetic canary inputs, not retrieved facts.
